News.title: Charming UK seaside town AXES summer fireworks display tonight – and replaces it with 200 AI-controlled drones
News.content:
A SEASIDE town’s weekly fireworks display will be replaced by 200 AI-powered drones this evening.

Organisers had initially chosen to cancel the event, but have insisted the “show will go on”.



Hundreds of LED drones will light up Great Yarmouth seafront tonight after organisers pulled its Big Wednesday firework display.

The town’s regular firework display runs as part of Visit Great Yarmouth’s summer calendar, however a national wildfire alert led to concerns.



Now, visitors will be able to witness 200 LED drones illuminate the skies above the seafront in a routine organised by international drone company, Lumina.

Chief executive of Visit Great Yarmouth, Asa Morrison, has insisted that the “show will go on” this evening.

“We are all thrilled to be able to put on unique entertainment for the thousands of people looking forward to spending their Wednesday evening on the seafront enjoying the vibrant fun family atmosphere and all that our businesses have to offer”, Morrison continued.

Organisers were also forced to cancel the Big Tuesday Night Fireworks on Hemsby Beach last night, and are set to update visitors about the upcoming events in due course.

Around 5,000 visitors flock to Norfolk’s famous Golden Mile beach every Wednesday of the summer holidays to enjoy an evening of live entertainment, street food and performances.

The decision was prompted by ongoing national wildfire concerns across the country, with over 1,000 recorded in England and Wales this year.



Millions of Brits received a phone alert on Friday warning of a “very high risk of wildfires” and urging them not to light barbecues, campfires, or fireworks.

Earlier this week, organisers of Britain’s biggest summer firework show in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, were forced to postpone the event until April to manage any wildfire risks.

Tonight, however, visitors will be able to catch a glimpse of the 200-powered drone show at 10pm, alongside an AeroSPARX coloured smoke plane display at dusk.

Chairman of Visit Great Yarmouth, Nathan Race, said: “Big Wednesdays are a much-loved part of the summer in Great Yarmouth and we know how much they mean to our visitors, residents and businesses.

“We are delighted to have found such an exciting alternative at very short notice.”

News.title: Dog food brand used by 40,000 Brits is urgently recalled as dozens of pets develop serious eye problems
News.content:
A PREMIUM dog food brand has urgently recalled its fresh meals after reports of eye problems in pets.

The company has warned all customers to not feed the meals to their pets or “any animals”.



Years, a subscription-based company specialising in fresh dog food, has temporarily paused all subscriptions after their buckwheat-based meals were found to be potentially linked with eye reactions in dogs.

According to the Press Association, around 57 dogs developed symptoms of keratoconjunctivitis sicca, known as bilateral dry eye, after consuming the wholefood products.



As a result, Years notified all 40,000 customers in an email on Monday (August 16) that it had removed the meals from circulation in a “voluntary recall” as the pet food undergoes lab testing.

The brand also launched a formal investigation into their signature meals, in collaboration with customers and veterinary professionals.



On its website, the firm wrote: “As a precaution, we’re issuing a voluntary recall of all Years Fresh Meals (excluding Chef’s Collection).

“This follows a small number of reports of dogs having a potential adverse eye reaction to buckwheat, a common and approved ingredient, which we include in our meals.

“As of 16th August, this has affected 0.1% of our customers.

“We know for some, this will strike as overly cautious – but at Years, we will always put every dog’s health and wellbeing first.”



They also urged customers to “stop feeding Years fresh meals immediately, whether your dog is experiencing symptoms or not” and to contact the support team if their pets have experienced dry eye symptoms at any point while on the subscription plan.

One affected customer, David Felton, from north London, said his dog Cookie had developed eye issues in April after eating the food for two-and-a-half years.

Speaking to the PA, he said he had spent around £1,500 on treatments, vet bills and medicines following his spaniel cross’s symptoms.

He said: “Never did it occur to us that it could be a link to the food because the crazy thing is people buy Years because they want to feed their dog like high quality foods.”

Dog owners have been warned to look out for redness, excessive blinking, a thick sticky mucus discharge and a dull or cloudy eye surface.



Persistent and untreated infections can leave pets with corneal ulcers, scarring and even permanent blindness.

Years Signature Meals had been stocked at major retailers, including Pets at Home and Just for Pets.

Now, the brand said it is reformulating its products to remove buckwheat, leading to subscriptions to be stopped for a precautionary six weeks.

It asked for the food to not be donated or sold, with the firm offering a free collection of any unused meals and full credit to be applied to affected accounts.

A spokesman for Years told the Falmouth Packet: “We’re sorry for the worry and disruption this will cause – both for the dogs affected and to all of our customers.



“We appreciate there will be other cases that have not been reported to Years.

“But even one case is one too many, and that’s the standard we will always hold ourselves to.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In time, we’d also welcome an open discussion with the wider veterinary and ophthalmologist community, to fund an independent study into how a common ingredient, like buckwheat could have led to such profound suffering in the dogs we love.”

Years has been approached for a comment.

News.title: Fury as 200-year-old ‘penis forest’ next to major UK motorway is CHOPPED down with just the tip left
News.content:
WOOD FOR THE TREES Fury as 200-year-old ‘penis forest’ next to major UK motorway is CHOPPED down with just the tip left

A 200-YEAR-OLD woodland dubbed the “Penis Woods” is being chopped down despite fury from fans of the phallic-shaped forest.

Castle Crawford Wood has been perched on Tewsgill Hill just off the M74 and ‘welcoming people to Scotland‘ for two centuries.



Plans to fell the woodland, known as the “Treenis” due to its distinctive outline, sparked outcry and a huge petition was launched to save it.

Locals said the trees should be a “protected landmark”.



But despite the swell of opposition, Scottish Forestry gave permission for its removal.

Pictures taken this week show work is almost already complete – with just the tip of the woods remaining.



Scottish Forestry said the wood had reached “the end of its natural lifecycle” and was experiencing “significant windblow” leaving many trees unstable.

The site, which is visible from the M74 motorway, has been felled and replanted several times throughout its history.



But the start of works has angered locals with a campaign to stop it now backed by over 2,700 signatures.

The petition starter wrote: “The Penis Woodland is a cultural landmark visible from the M74 in Scotland.

“This iconic cultivation is going to be felled.

“It’s not just any woodland, it’s a penis shaped woodland, visible from the motorway.”

The shepherd in charge of the day-to-day running of the farm, said in a statement: “We feel for the safe keeping of the wood itself it has to be done sooner rather than later as the damage will get worse and it will look nothing like a ‘T’ in a few years if we don’t.



“We plan to get it back to its former glory ASAP. This is not for any financial gain, once-replanted and fenced it will probably leave a loss.

“There’s a lots of trees down which will be rotting and a lot that are still standing are dying swell.

“We’ve sorted these things before but eventually comes a time where you need to cut your losses and completely fell it and start again. If you want it to have any chance of staying the shape it is for hundreds of years to come it’s the only way to do it.



“The trees that are healthy are a fair height and now that there is so much space for wind to get at them by the time you planted more and the time it takes them to grow the big trees would be down on top of them in the next storm”.

Castle Crawford Wood was originally planted in the 1800s, and features on maps dating back as far as 1849.

Several comments were also left on the petition by supporters of the wood.

One wrote: “These trees should be a protected landmark, as something of cultural significance.”

Another added: “This stretch of woodland is not only a memorable and wonderful landmark for those who have seen and visited it but holds so much life within that would otherwise be lost with its destruction.”



A spokesman for Scottish Forestry said: “Castle Crawford Wood, which was originally planted in the late 1800s, has reached the end of its natural lifecycle and is experiencing significant windblow, leaving many remaining trees unstable and at risk of further failure.

“Following assessment and public consultation, Scottish Forestry has approved the felling of the woodland, which is in progress.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This forms part of the wood’s long-established management, with the site having been felled and replanted several times throughout its history.

“The area is required to be restocked with an appropriate mix of trees species, helping to ensure a sustainable woodland long-term.”

News.title: Moment dog leads cops to fugitive owner’s hiding place after he fled officers on e-scooter and left hero pooch behind
News.content:
THIS is the moment a dog led cops to his fugitive owner after he fled officers and left the Labrador behind.

Charles Foy had escaped on his e-scooter after police stopped him for riding the vehicle illegally in Runcorn, Cheshire, with his two dogs running alongside him.



But the 41-year-old’s Labrador could not keep up with the scooter and was left behind.

The clever pooch was then filmed leading police to his owner.



Footage shows officers calling the dog a “good boy” as he walks down the street with them in tow.

After leading the cops back to his owner’s house, the Lab then hops into a police car after a job well done.



Bodycam then shows officers hunting through the home for Foy, who was hiding out in a loft.

After he was rumbled, one cop told him: “Get out, get out now. You know you’ve done something, that’s why you’re hiding in the loft, get down.”



Foy then yelled back: “Calm the f*** down. I’ve been trying to get some sleep.”

He also claimed he was asleep in the loft due to the overcrowded nature of the property and had not been out riding the e-scooter that night.

Foy was later convicted of failing to stop for police, driving whilst disqualified, using a motor vehicle without insurance and failing to provide a drug test.

He has now been jailed for three months and banned from driving for four years and three months.

PC Mike Smith, of Runcorn Response, said: “Whilst Foy showed no loyalty to his own dog as he attempted to make good his escape from pursuing police, the pup ultimately remained loyal and provided us with a vital lead – taking us straight to the address of his master.



“The custodial sentence and the four-plus-year road ban handed to Foy reflects the serious nature of the offences he committed. Not only did he appear to be riding under the influence of substances that could severely impair his reaction times, but the fact of the matter is that he was riding an illegal vehicle that can reach considerable speeds in a matter of seconds and can have devastating effects should a collision occur.

“Vehicles like e-scooters and e-bike cannot be ridden on public roads due to the fact that they cannot be insured.

“In these cases, they may actually be classed as a motor vehicle, meaning the rider would need a licence, insurance and a helmet – something many riders like Foy do not possess.”

News.title: Mushroom killer Erin Patterson’s lawyers reveal ‘catastrophic’ blunder in last-ditch effort to overturn murder sentence
News.content:
MUSHROOM killer Erin Patterson’s lawyers have revealed a “catastrophic” blunder from her trial in a last-ditch bid to quash her life sentence.

The triple murderer was jailed for life with a non-parole period of 33 years for serving her in-laws poisoned beef Wellingtons laced with death cap mushrooms.



Her mum-in-law Gail Patterson, dad-in-law Donald Patterson and Gail’s sister Heather Wilkinson died in hospital within six days of the fatal lunch in July 2023.

Patterson, 51, was also convicted for the attempted murder of Heather’s husband, Ian Wilkinson, a small-town local pastor who miraculously survived the poisoning.



Her legal team have now begun their appeal to quash her convictions and order a retrial, with Patterson appearing at court via video link from behind bars.

Barrister Richard Edney slammed the “catastrophic” decision to place members of the jury in the same hotel as a police witness, journalists and members of the prosecution.



Edney argued that the move “fatally undermined the integrity of the verdicts” and means the verdicts should be quashed and a retrial should take place “so that justice can be done”.

The court heard that, despite Edney’s complaints, there was no evidence that the jury came into contact with anyone at trial.



Edney said: “This was a hotel with windows, with common areas and the reasonable possibility cannot be excluded that the jurors sighted the informant or sighted solicitors from the Office of Public Prosecutions.”

Justice Peter Kidd instantly challenged the submission, saying: “If they did view or see the practitioners, so what?”

While the defence acknowledged that there was no evidence that the jury spoke with the witness or prosecution, they highlighted that the crossover occurred during jury deliberation week.



Another contentious point concerned the prosecution’s use of evidence about Patterson’s activity on the foraging website iNaturalist and mobile phone tower data.

At the trial, the prosecution argued that Patterson found two sightings of death cap mushrooms reported online near her home.

The court heard how her phone connected to cell towers in both areas, with the prosecution indicating she’d visited both spots.

Hours after visiting one of the locations, Patterson bought a food dehydrator to prepare the mushrooms for the fateful beef Wellingtons.

CCTV captured Patterson travelling to a local dump and disposing of the dehydrator, which was later found to have traces of the deadly mushrooms.



When sentencing Patterson, the judge said that it didn’t necessarily matter where she sourced the mushrooms from as it was abundantly clear that she had.

Patterson has maintained she unknowingly used foraged death cap mushrooms in the meal.

'MUSHROOM' MURDER TIMELINE All the twists & turns that led to Erin Patterson being jailed for life 2021-22 – A 48-year-old man, believed to Patterson’s ex-husband Simon, falls ill after three separate meails. July 29, 2023 – The deadly mushroom lunch takes place July 30 – Gail and Don Patterson & Heather and Ian Wilkinson are rushed to hospital – all die but Ian. August 5-7 – Patterson’s home is searched, she is questions and becomes an official suspect. November 2 – Police arrest and charge Patterson with three counts of murder and five of attempted murder. May 7, 2024 – Patterson pleads not guilty to the eight charges. April 29, 2025 – Her trial begins. The prosecuction drop three charges related to the attempted murder of Simon. July 7, 2025 – The jury finds Patterson guilty. September 8, 2025 – She is sentenced to life imprisonment with a non-parole period of 33 years.

However, Ian Wilkinson, the sole survivor of the lunch, told the trial that Patterson served guests individual portions, separate from her own.

Toxicologists confirmed all four guests displayed symptoms consistent with death cap mushroom poisoning, a highly lethal species found in the local area.

Symptoms can begin within hours of ingestion and include severe vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain.



In the most serious cases, they can temporarily subside before returning days later, often leading to liver and kidney failure and death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police have also alleged Patterson may have attempted to poison her ex-husband, Simon Patterson, on three separate occasions between 2021 and 2022.

Simon previously wrote about a near-fatal illness that left him in a coma for 16 days, during which doctors advised his family to prepare for the worst.

News.title: Sister of TikTok star, 29, found dead in remote vineyard fears she may ‘have run into wrong guy at wrong time’
News.content:
DEATH PROBE Sister of TikTok star, 29, found dead in remote vineyard fears she may ‘have run into wrong guy at wrong time’

THE grieving sister of a TikTok star found dead in a remote vineyard fears she “may have run into the wrong guy” as French cops launch a murder probe.

Sonia Bellina, 29, vanished while on holiday in Southern France on August 10.



Her naked and partially burnt body was found at an isolated vineyard in Saint-Gilles, near Nimes, two days later.

Bellina’s sister, who asked for her name not to be published, recalled the events of August 10, saying: “She said she was going out one evening, and she never came back.”



She said her sister may have “run into the wrong guy at the wrong time,” without providing further details.

Her sister told the Midi Libre news outlet: “I never thought something like this would happen to our family, especially since she was such a radiant, kind person whom everyone loved.



“I am shocked to be living in such a cruel world. This is a terrible injustice. We don’t deserve to go through this.

“We were getting ready for her birthday—she would have turned 30 on September 30th – and we had planned to throw a party.”



The victim’s family also condemned a sickening “hate campaign” on social media which followed news of Bellina’s death.

Her sister said: “People are going too far – it’s awful, and they’re coming out with nonsense.

“It’s harassment – some are even saying she deserved what happened to her. People are using my sister’s photos just to generate a buzz.”

The popular influencer had more than a quarter-of-a-million followers on TikTok, and was known for sharing details of her life across multiple social media platforms, where she also used the name Mia.

Members of her family identified her body after a farm worker made the horrific discovery.



Cécile Gensac, the Nimes public prosecutor later confirmed the launching of a murder inquiry.

He said: “The body was found lying between rows of vines.”

Ms Gensac said the body had been “partially burned,” in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence.

There have been no arrests in connection with the inquiry so far.

Mourad Battikh, the lawyer representing the Bellina family, who live in Nimes, said: “The family is going through an ordeal of extreme severity.



“They condemn the publication of rumours, speculation, offensive remarks, and accusations, accompanied by images and details concerning their private lives.

“My firm is already taking steps to document and preserve evidence. Depending on the specific case, each publication will trigger reports to the platforms.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Law and order officials frequently issue warnings to influencers and others who post details of their lives to strangers, saying they can attract unwanted attention from criminals, including stalkers.

The enquiry into the death of Sonia Bellina continues.

News.title: What time are the 2026 GCSE results released and can you get your grades online?
News.content:
FOR hundreds of thousands of teenagers the next step depends on what GCSE results they get on Thursday morning.

Here’s the exact time grades are released, and whether you can see yours without leaving the house.



What time do GCSE results come out in 2026?

GCSE grades are released to students from 8am on Thursday, August 20.

That is the earliest moment schools are allowed to hand anything over, not a national release time – some open their doors later in the morning.



Schools receive the results a day earlier, from just after midnight on Wednesday, August 19, but are under a strict embargo until Thursday.

Staff are banned from discussing grades with students, parents, other teachers or anyone else before then, and any breach counts as malpractice.



The date is set by the Joint Council for Qualifications (JCQ) and covers every board, including AQA, Pearson Edexcel, OCR, WJEC and CCEA.

Entry-level certificates, foundation and higher projects and most Level 1 and 2 vocational technical qualifications all arrive the same morning.

Can you check GCSE results online?

Some students can log in and see their GCSE grades online, but there is no national website where you enter a candidate number and get your results.

Exam boards don’t issue paper results anymore – electronic files are sent to schools.



Each school then decides how to pass them on, whether that means printed slips, an email or a login to its own system.

Emailed results are also allowed, but not before 8am.

Where schools do use online portals, access is usually limited to the student rather than parents, and some close the system within a fortnight.

So the answer depends entirely on where you sat your exams – ask your exams officer before Thursday rather than assuming.

Can someone else pick up your results for you?

Most schools will allow it, but only if you arrange it beforehand.



Typically that means a letter signed by the student naming the person collecting being handed to the exams officer before results day, with the nominated adult bringing photo ID on the morning.

Some schools accept an email sent directly from the student, although many refuse text messages or a photos of a signed note.

Policies on posting uncollected results also differ – some send them out that same afternoon, while others will not post them under any circumstances.

What do GCSE grades mean?

England uses the 9 to 1 scale, where 9 is the highest grade and 4 is broadly a standard pass.

Grade 4 is around the bottom end of the old C grade, with grade 5 a strong pass sitting between a high C and a low B.



Wales has stuck with letter grades, while students in Northern Ireland may receive either system or a combination of both.

What can you do if you think your grade is wrong?

A review of marking comes first, which checks whether the mark scheme was applied correctly rather than marking the paper afresh.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Requests have to go through your school, so the exams officer is the first person to speak to, and written consent is needed because marks can fall as well as rise.

Boards must receive requests by Thursday, September 24, 2026, and you then have 30 calendar days from the outcome to lodge a formal appeal.

News.title: Teen woman among three arrested after pensioner, 81, found dead in burnt-out campervan on Christmas Day
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

OAP HORROR Teen woman among three arrested after pensioner, 81, found dead in burnt-out campervan on Christmas Day

A TEENAGE woman and two others have been arrested after a pensioner was found dead in a burnt-out caravan on Christmas Day.

Godfrey Bradford, 81, was found at the dead scene when police arrived at March Lane in Chudleigh just before 11am on December 25, 2025.

A 19-year-old woman and an 18-year-old man have now been arrested on suspicion of murder.

A woman in her 50s was also arrested on suspicion of intentionally encouraging/assisting the commission of murder.





All three suspects are from South Devon and have been released on bail, Devon and Cornwall Police said.

Emergency services raced to the scene following concerns for a man.

The fire had been extinguished by the time they arrived and officers found the body of the retired farm contractor in the fire-ravaged campervan.

DI Chris Lithgow from the Major Crime Investigation Team, said: “Our officers have carried out three arrests as part of our enquiries into the death of Godfrey Bradford near Chudleigh on Christmas Day last year.



“The arrests follow months of investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr Bradford’s death.

“We would like to remind the public not to speculate on what is an ongoing investigation.”

A spokesperson for the force added: “Officers were called at 10.50am on 25 December 2025 to a rural property north of Chudleigh following concerns for a man.

“Emergency services attended the scene where a fire was believed to have occurred.



“A man was located in the property and was confirmed deceased at the scene.

“He was later identified as 81-year-old local man Godfrey Bradford.”

News.title: Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as controversial star issues grovelling apology
News.content:
Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as controversial star issues grovelling apology

Nick Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in Mallorca June, with the Australian now admitting that he made a 'huge mistake' and pledging to 'come back better'

View Image Nick Kyrgios has apologised following his provisional ban (Image: TPN/Getty Images)

Tennis star Nick Kyrgios has issued a grovelling apology after testing positive for cocaine. Kyrgios, 31, has been provisionally suspended following the test which took place at the ATP 250 tournament in Mallorca in June.

‌



His International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) provisional suspension has been in place since August 4. Kyrgios has the right to appeal the ban but is yet to do so.

‌



The Australian wrote on his Instagram story: "I wanted you to hear this from me first. I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine. I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

‌



"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Emma Raducanu could QUIT tennis over injury hell, claims BBC icon READ MORE :

Carlos Alcaraz issued US Open warning as injury comeback plans in balance READ MORE :

"I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

‌



"I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did.

"However, the good news is that this has given me a wake up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

"I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family. I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick."

Article continues below

Under the terms of his suspension, Kyrgios cannot play, coach at or even attend any Grand Slams or events sanctioned by the men's and women's tennis tours. The 31-year-old has been restricted to just four singles matches this season, with knee and wrist injuries hampering his career in recent years.

Kyrgios last played at Wimbledon in the men's doubles. He partnered Kazakhstan's Alexander Bublik but they were knocked out in the first round, losing to Mate Pavic and Marcelo Arevalo.

News.title: Met Office names six counties facing storms and power cuts in 12-hour warning
News.content:
Met Office names six counties facing storms and power cuts in 12-hour warning

The Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for thunderstorms which is due to come into force at midday today, with Brits facing power cuts and flooding

View 2 Images Thunderstorms are coming to some parts of the UK (stock) (Image: PA)

The Met Office has issued a weather warning as thunderstorms are set to batter parts of the UK today.

‌



The yellow warning covers Nothern Ireland and will come into force at midday, lasting until midnight.

‌



As well as heavy rain, thunder, lightning and hail, the national weather agency says there is a risk of power cuts. "Some flooding of a few homes and businesses [is] likely" too, the warning adds.

‌



Delays to train services are also on the cards. "Some short-term loss of power and other services is likely" as well.

The weather warning states as much as 20mm of rain is likely in an hour or less, with a few places possibly seeing 30mm across a couple of hours.

View 2 Images The warning has been issued for Northern Ireland (Image: Met Office)

‌

The Met Office is urging people in the warning area to get ready for floods by "preparing a flood plan and an emergency flood kit".

People should also get ready for power cuts by "gathering torches and batteries, a mobile phone power pack and other essential items".

Heavy showers are expected in northern areas later in the day, "especially in the north where hail and thunder possible", with more heavy rain coming in northern England and North Wales tonight.

News.title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36: Ex Brian Hickerson at scene when she died as mum breaks silence
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, with the initial investigation from police finding there was 'no foul play' and autopsy results confirming 'no signs of trauma'

US actress Hayden Panettiere, who was best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. Her death was confirmed by her representatives and followed by a statement.

The statement from her father, Skip, read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

Meanwhile, her mother spoke the first time on Tuesday, firing shots at ex Brian Hickerson. She said: "I think Hayden was an amazingly talented person in so many departments and I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry -- it is a struggle and it's a very challenging industry and it's not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path."

She also added: "This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death, and that was Brian Hickerson."

The Coroner's office confirmed that Hayden's autopsy showed 'no signs of trauma' at the time of her death. It had been reported that the police were responding to a call about a suspected "cardiac arrest". A police report later revealed that both her ex Hickerson and his brother Zach were at the scene at the time of her death.

911 audio footage also heard dispatchers discuss a suspected overdose. Both Narcan and Epinephrine were reportedly brought to the scene by emergency services Panettiere's cause of death has not been announced at this time.

A preliminary police investigation has confirmed there were no signs of "foul play or suspicious circumstances" when they arrived at her home after a 911 emergency call from an acquaintance of Panettiere's.

News.title: Popular sun cream declared 'high risk' now 'banned from sale' in UK
News.content:
Popular sun cream declared 'high risk' now 'banned from sale' in UK

The products have been rejected at the UK border

View 2 Images A popular brand of sun cream has been rejected at the UK border (Image: Carlos Barquero/Getty)

A popular brand of sun cream has been branded "high risk". The Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) has issued a notice for the product, stating it was rejected at the UK border.

‌



Bubble Cosmetics Sunscreen Pack has been given a "high risk" rating by the OPSS. It said: "The product presents a risk due to inadequate labelling and traceability information.

‌



"Multiple mandatory cosmetic labelling requirements have not been met, including omissions relating to sunscreen use instructions and product traceability. As a result, consumers may not have sufficient information to use the product appropriately, and effective regulatory traceability is impaired."

‌



It added: "The product does not meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 (‘the Cosmetics Regulation’)." As a result, the products have been rejected for entry into the UK and therefore cannot be sold to customers.

View 2 Images Bubble Cosmetics Sunscreen Pack has been recalled (Image: OPSS)

The sun cream came from the United States. Bubble is sold in a range of UK retailers, including Boots and Asos. The affected items are a range of Bubble sun cream products packaged in yellow cardboard boxes.

‌



The Mirror has contacted Bubble for comment.

Earlier this month, a brand of wet wipes was urgently recalled due to contamination risks. The OPSS explained that the wipes may be microbiologically contaminated, meaning they could cause adverse skin reactions.

FreshWipes Intimate Unscented Wipes were sold on the FreshWipes website, Amazon UK, TG Jones (formerly WH Smith), TikTok Shop and QVC. It is described as a 10-pack of moist wipes, which are also sold in multipacks and in self-care bundles.

‌



The OPSS said: "It has been identified that affected batches may be microbiologically contaminated, with the preservative system not performing as required.

"This could result in users experiencing adverse skin reactions. The affected batches do not meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 (the ‘Cosmetics Regulation’).

"The product has been recalled from end users by FreshWipes. Consumers who have an affected batch should stop using the product immediately. Contact your place of purchase for instructions on return or disposal of product and refund/redress."

Article continues below

FreshWipes said: "Check the batch number printed on the back of the pack. If it reads LOT 0926 or LOT 0515, the product is part of this recall.

"What to do: Please stop using the affected product immediately. If you have purchased Freshwipes Intimate Wipes from Batch LOT 0926 or LOT 0515, please contact our customer support team at Sales@freshwipes.co.uk with a photo of your remaining packs clearly showing the LOT number.

"We apologise for any inconvenience caused and remain committed to the safety and quality of our products."

News.title: Accused 'paedophile' found dead below cliff after not turning up to hear court verdict
News.content:
Accused 'paedophile' found dead below cliff after not turning up to hear court verdict

David John Grover, 72, absconded from a trial where he faced serious sexual allegations and was found dead at the bottom of the cliff in Cornwall

View 2 Images The emergency services in Mousehole on the day Mr Grover's body was recovered (Image: Jacob Harvey)

A man accused of being a paedophile was found dead at the bottom of a cliff 400 miles from his home - and his family say he had been "destroyed" by "false allegations".

David John Grover, 72, from Margate in Kent, was discovered on rocks at the bottom of the cliff at Mousehole, Cornwall last winter after he absconded from a trial.

His body was spotted by walkers on November 22, which prompted a massive emergency response. Coastguard cliff rescue teams and RNLI crews searched the cliff and water below.

Mr Grover had been due to hear the verdict in his trial at Canterbury Crown Court the day before but failed to attend court, and a high risk missing person warrant was issued by police in Kent, Cornwall Live reports.

View 2 Images Mr Grover was found dead in Mousehole, Cornwall - 400 miles from his home (file) (Image: Getty Images)

He took a taxi to Margate train station, withdrew £200 in cash and travelled by train to St Pancras in London before being found dead in Mousehole near Penzance the next day.

An inquest into his death held in Truro on Tuesday heard how Mr Grover's health started deteriorating as allegations of a sexual nature were made against him two years prior to his death.

Mr Grover faced three counts of indecent assault, one of sexual assault and a fifth charge of inciting a child to engage in sexual activity in connection with an alleged sexual assault on a female under the age of 14 three decades prior.

His daughter Sherie Seal told the coroner's court how her father had a great personality and sense of humour, and had been a proud man who was loved by his family and friends.

She told the hearing how he loved bowling and was the captain of the Margate bowling club. He had a dog whom he had raised from pup and enjoyed playing chess or board games with his grandchildren.

She said: "His overall health deteriorated when false allegations were made against him that happened 30 years ago. That caused him sleepless nights."

Mrs Seal said she attended the trial every day to be by her father's side and support him through the ordeal. She added: "He had already been destroyed the day false allegations were made... On the day of the closing statements you could see that my dad was broken. He was very quiet and distant. I told him it would be okay."

She told the inquest how her father still could not believe the allegations made against him and believes he was badly treated by police investigating the allegations. "Dad was a strong living man and he was ruined by an unhinged, lying fantasist," she said.

The inquest heard Mr Grover had booked a short stay at the Queen's Hotel on Penzance Promenade the week before his trial had been due to start, and he was familiar with the area.

A police investigation found Mr Grover had last been seen in court the day before his death but absconded on the day the jury was due to give its verdict.

He was discovered dead in Mousehole the next day having concealed his digital presence by withdrawing £200 in cash instead of paying for anything with cards. A postmortem examination showed Mr Grover drowned.

The police officer investigating the circumstances of Mr Grover's death said no third party or suspicious circumstances were involved.

Andrew Cox, senior coroner for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, said that while he was the subject of an ongoing criminal trial, no conclusion had yet been reached and no conviction.

Article continues below

He said: "The jury had not returned its verdict. On the last day of the trial, Mr Grover took a taxi to the train station and then the train to St Pancras in London. What happened after that, we don't know. He travelled from London to Cornwall and Penzance but there is no evidence of how he did it, whether he took the train or hitched a lift.

"There is no evidence of how he came to be in the sea and drowned. The obvious implication is that he died from suicide but there is a huge gap in the evidence with nothing that explains how he went from London to Cornwall and what happened when he arrived in Penzance."

In the absence of conclusive evidence on how Mr Grover came by his death, Mr Cox recorded an open conclusion.

News.title: Match of the Day chaos as BBC 'fear mass exodus' of top pundits after clashes emerge
News.content:
Match of the Day chaos as BBC 'fear mass exodus' of top pundits after clashes emerge

More pundits could be following Gary Lineker out of the Match of the Day exit door

View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates took over as Match of the Day presenters in 2025 (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC / Charlie Clift)

The BBC is at risk of a mass exodus of pundits with fears growing on the eve of the new Premier League season, it has been claimed. It comes just one year after the broadcaster changed its presenting team for flagship football show Match of the Day, with Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan now sharing presenting duties.

‌



Cates, Chapman and Logan took over after Gary Lineker's 25-year stint with the Beeb was brought to an end. Lineker brought his The Rest is Football show to Netflix during the World Cup and has agreed a deal with the streaming service to stay there for the next two Premier League seasons.

‌



According to The Sun, a number of Match of the Day pundits have been weighing up whether to leave for Lineker's new show after Alan Shearer and Micah Richards divided their time between the two during the World Cup. The same publication alleges there have been clashes between BBC head of sport Alex Kay-Jelski and unnamed members of the Match of the Day team.

‌



The same report points to the deal signed between Gary Neville and Disney+ for The Overlap's podcast content, suggesting this too could offer pundits alternatives to Match of the Day. The BBC said in a statement: “We have repeatedly told The Sun these anonymous claims are untrue and we look forward to bringing audiences the return of Match of the Day this weekend with its established line-up of presenters and pundits – alongside a host of new guest voices bringing fresh insight from inside the game.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Kelly Cates makes thoughts clear on Gabby Logan and Mark Chapman as she opens up on BBC job READ MORE :

Mark Chapman's BBC colleagues have all told World Cup host exactly what they think of him READ MORE :

Lineker had initially been slated to present the BBC's World Cup coverage even after leaving Match of the Day. However this changed when he walked away in May 2025 amid backlash to a social media post and he has since spoken about his life away from the Beeb.

‌



"I've got a bit more time, I'm not treading on quite so many eggshells these days, I'm allowed an opinion on things.," he told the Press Association ahead of the tournament in North America

"But no, I had a wonderful period at the Beeb, and I've covered so many major tournaments, and obviously I was going to do this (the 2026 World Cup) originally, but now I'm doing something different, which is really exciting."

While the latest reports point to a fear of further pundit exits, there have also been suggestions of a new addition. Former Tottenham and Belgium defender Toby Alderweireld, who retired from playing in 2025, is reportedly being lined up to join the Match of the Day punditry roster.

‌



View 2 Images Gary Lineker has been joined by Micah Richards and Alan Shearer on The Rest is Football (Image: Netflix/PA Wire)

At the end of last season, new presenter Cates told Mirror Football about her admiration for the behind-the-scenes team involved in Match of the Day. The presenter has also hosted Sky Sports coverage but appeared positive when discussing her new role.

“Match of the Day is bigger than the presenters,” she said. “I think that's what I've learned, that all the people who work behind the scenes to kind of keep everything on it, they're the people who make the programme what it is.

Article continues below

“Viewers really watch for the football. They're not watching for anything else. I've worked with [the Match of the Day pundits] before. There's nobody who's been brand new to me, that was really nice, but that helps me and it just helps to have some continuity.”
