La Junta de Andalucía mantiene activa la fase de preemergencia del plan ante el riesgo sísmico desde el seísmo registrado la madrugada del pasado sábado, de magnitud 5 y con epicentro en Alhendín. Por su parte, el Servicio Andaluz de Salud, dependiente de la Consejería de Presidencia, Sanidad y Emergencias, ha informado de que la actividad asistencial se ha restablecido “con normalidad” después de la “suspensión temporal y preventiva” acordada para facilitar la evaluación de las instalaciones y garantizar la seguridad de pacientes y profesionales.

La Alhambra reabre sin la Alcazaba

La Alhambra, el conjunto monumental históricamente más visitado del país, reabre este miércoles al público con los itinerarios por los Palacios Nazaríes y el Generalife adaptados para garantizar la seguridad de los visitantes y facilitar una evacuación ágil si fuera necesario. Después del desalojo el martes de parte de las instalaciones, la Alcazaba permanece cerrada hasta nuevo aviso.

World.title: Santiago de Compostela quiere tirar a los peregrinos al pilón
World.content:
Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las columnas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

Abundan este verano los vídeos de grupos de peregrinos que entran a Santiago de Compostela demostrando que el camino les ha hecho mejores, más reflexivos, más conscientes, más sutiles y más sabios. Se les nota en la manera de berrear canciones de charanga e intimidar a los peatones, en el ansia con la que se embaulan las cervezas en los muy espirituales bares de la zona y en el vigor con el que las orinan luego por las esquinas del casco histórico.

Tanta devoción cristiana y tanto fervor introspectivo tienen a los vecinos del centro de la capital gallega en un estado de ateísmo radical y nihilismo. Más de uno ha estado a punto de arrojar desde el balcón las obras completas de Nietzsche en tapa dura al paso de los buenos peregrinos: si no les convencemos de que Dios ha muerto —dicen—, por lo menos, descalabraremos a dos o tres. Deploremos la violencia filosófica, pero concedámosles nuestra simpatía. Yo tenía costumbre de ir todos los años a dar una vuelta por Santiago, aunque ya no me acerco. Un poco por miedo a los peregrinos, y otro poco por miedo a que me confundan con uno y me tiren a alguno de los pilones románicos que aún conservan en las plazas.

El odio al turista es la cantinela de los sitios turísticos, pero en Santiago se vuelve paradoja. Porque la ciudad solo existe por el Camino. La fundó un rey asturiano en torno al sepulcro, con la esperanza de atraer el turismo a una zona deprimida de su reino, y un par de siglos después, la orden de Cluny, que era el Meliá de la época, montó una cadena de alojamientos muy cucos y convenientes para quitarle el turismo a Roma y llevarlo a Galicia. Dice Álvarez Junco que por entonces apareció el gentilicio “español”, palabra francesa con la que los turistas designaban a los que vivían al sur de los Pirineos y les sacaban los cuartos en el camino con la venta de vino malo y productos regionales.

Santiago y España tienen un origen turístico. Cuando se dice que el turismo pervierte las esencias de las ciudades y de los países hay que hacer algunas excepciones, y Santiago es de las más gruesas. Por mucho que irriten, esos peregrinos charangueros representan el espíritu primordial de la ciudad. Le recuerdan lo que es, como las ovejas que cruzan Madrid una vez al año para que nadie olvide que la Castellana es una cañada. En este caso, quizá no haya más remedio que pedirle al apóstol paciencia para soportar el verano. Y a los peregrinos, menos fervor.

World.title: Dutch media attack “chilling” fines for slimming drugs coverage
World.content:
Dutch media companies have been hit with fines running into the tens of millions of euros after inspectors ruled that their reporting on weight loss drugs such as Ozempic amounted to advertising.

Editors described the penalties, issued by the health department’s inspectorate IGJ, as “bizarre” and an attack on press freedom.

The verdicts covered newspapers across the range and political spectrum of Dutch media including NRC, the Volkskrant, the Telegraaf and AD.

The inspectors said the coverage of medicines such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro was too positive because it reported that the benefits of the drugs went beyond treating diabetes, the only condition they are prescribed for in the Netherlands.

The Dutch Medicines Act bans advertising for prescription medicines. The IGJ said it had issued around 20 fines between 2023 for breaching the law, not just to media companies.

Science reporting

The inspectorate would not go into individual cases, but DPG Media, one of the two main news publishers in the Netherlands, said it had been fined €48,500 in April for two articles in local newspaper De Stentor and lifestyle magazine Flair, and another €51,000 this month for articles in the Volkskrant and AD.

Mediahuis was fined a total of €132,000 this month for articles in NRC’s science section and the Telegraaf.

The IGJ said: “We weigh up the facts carefully in each case, including the interests of patients. In the case of media coverage we look at the whole picture: content, context, images and audio. It’s not a tick list.”

The journalists’ union NVJ said it was “shocked” that the inspectorate had imposed fines on reporters “who regularly write about medicines and have no other interest than informing the public.”

General secretary Thomas Bruning called for talks with the health ministry to discuss the sanctions. “This makes it impossible for journalists to report on this subject in a normal fashion,” he said. “We are taking it very seriously.”

Press freedom

Pieter Klok, editor of the Volkskrant, said he respected the ban on advertising and the IGJ’s right to enforce it. “But I don’t think it should be applied to journalism, unless you can show it’s been paid for,” he said.

Telegraaf editor Kamran Ullah said it would have a “huge chilling effect” on journalists reporting on health issues.

“That goes not just for large news organisations like us, but maybe even more for smaller titles and freelancers. Big publishers can pay these fines, but a fine of more than €100,000 is the equivalent of two journalists’ annual salary.

“That’s a real infringement of press freedom, because if we have to pay these fines, we can’t employ as many journalists.”

World.title: AI share prices lift household investments to a record high
World.content:
Dutch households’ investments in the stock market are worth more than ever amid the boom in enthusiasm around AI and technology, the central bank DNB has said.

The total value of shares, funds and bonds held by Dutch households rose about 12% in the second quarter to a record €234.2 billion. It is the sharpest rise in a single quarter since the bank started tracking the figures in 2018.

The gain was almost entirely down to rising share prices, which lifted the value of investments people already owned. Households did not buy more shares – over the quarter they actually sold more than they bought.

ASML, Shell and SpaceX

The fervour around AI adoption has helped ASML, the chip-machine maker, become the most valuable holding in Dutch portfolios, at about €6.1 billion. It pushed Shell, long the most popular investment, into second place at around €4.1 billion, with Rabobank third.

The quarter also saw a massive stock-market debut with Elon Musk’s space company SpaceX listed in New York in June, with Dutch households buying €169 million of its shares in the first month – the most they have ever put into a newly listed company since DNB’s records began.

Many did not hold on for long. A large part was sold again within weeks, probably to lock in the early gains, leaving €71 million still invested by the end of June.

Despite all the gains, investing remains a minority practice in the Netherlands. Only about a quarter of the country’s 8.4 million households invest at all, and the Dutch still keep far more in the bank – around €600 billion in savings – than in the markets.

World.title: Berendsen: Netherlands “disapproves” of new Trump ICC sanctions
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch foreign minister Tom Berendsen has criticised the latest sanctions imposed by the Trump administration against officials of the International Criminal Court, based in The Hague.

Berendsen said international courts “must be able to freely carry out their mandates” after the measures were taken against the court’s president, Tomoko Akane, and senior prosecutor Abdoulaye Saye.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Akane and Saye had been “directly engaged in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government ⁠has not consented to ICC jurisdiction.”

Seye was a member of the prosecution team that drafted the arrest warrants against Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s former defence minister Yoav Gallant 18 months ago.

Shortly afterwards Donald Trump issued an executive order authorising sanctions against ICC officials, such as freezing their bank accounts in the US and shutting them out of international payment systems.

The US and Israel are not signatories to the ICC’s founding statutes, but the government of Palestine is. The ICC ruled in 2021 that Gaza and the West Bank fell under its jurisdiction.

Continued support

Berendsen said in a post on social media site X, formerly Twitter: “The Netherlands disapproves of the latest sanctions against officials and staff of the International Criminal Court.”

He went on to offer to meet Akane “to discuss our continued support.” Berendsen did not directly condemn the US government’s actions.

The Netherlands disapproves of the latest sanctions against officials and staff of the International Criminal Court. International courts and tribunals must be able to freely carry out their mandates. 1/2 — Tom Berendsen (@ministerBZ) August 18, 2026



Akane said last year that the sanctions would “rapidly undermine the court’s operations”, while in recent months Rubio has stepped up his rhetoric against the ICC, accusing it of “waging a war against our country” and vowing to dismantle it “brick by brick”.

World.title: Higher oil prices drive up Dutch industrial turnover
World.content:
Dutch industrial turnover rose 8.4% in the second quarter, the biggest year-on-year rise since the end of 2022. But it was driven mainly by higher oil prices rather than a real recovery, figures from national statistics agency CBS show.

Prices across industry were 5% higher than a year ago, so more than half of the rise reflects costlier goods rather than higher sales. Last year, turnover had fallen 0.7%.

The growth was also uneven, with refineries and the chemical industry taking in 31.2% more than a year earlier, and the oil industry alone up 83% as its selling prices rose 40.5%.

The higher oil prices stem from disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been largely shut since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. With few ships getting through, prices have risen – the same reason petrol has been so expensive in the Netherlands this year.

Not every sector grew. Food, drink and tobacco fell furthest, with turnover down 6.7%, mainly because selling prices dropped. Shoppers are unlikely to see that in the supermarket yet, as there are many steps between factory and shelf.

Manufacturers are more optimistic about the months ahead, with more expecting higher turnover than at any point since mid-2022. Even so, many still cannot find enough workers, and slightly more industrial companies went bankrupt than a year earlier, CBS said.

World.title: “Exceptional” 17th-century sketchbook donated to Rijksmuseum
World.content:
A 17th-century sketchbook containing 30 drawings has been hailed as a rare find after it was donated to the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

Several of the sketches have been attributed to the Frisian painter Rombould Uylenburgh, who was a well-known artist in his day but fell into obscurity following his death in 1627 or 1628.

The book is known as the Van Eeghen sketchbook, after the family of Amsterdam merchants who owned it for three centuries. The sketches, some of which were made on blue paper, have retained their colour because the book has not been on display.

The Rijksmuseum said it was unusual for an artist’s sketchbook from the 17th century to survive intact for so long. More commonly, the drawings are torn out and sold individually, or lost.

Only two sketches and a handful of paintings by Uylenburgh were thought to have survived when the sketchbook resurfaced in 1935.

The drawings in the book were only attributed to him in 2013, after the owner saw they were similar to one of the artist’s works in the Rijksmuseum’s collection.

Uylenburgh was born in Friesland in 1580 but spent most of his life in Poland after his family emigrated to Krakow. He because the court painter of King Sigismund III Vasa and went on to build a successful career in the port city of Danzig.

His brother, Hendrik, returned to the Dutch Republic and based himself in Amsterdam. By 1625 had established himself as Rembrandt’s main art dealer and is believed to have introduced the painter to his cousin, Saskia van Uylenburgh, who married Rembrandt in 1633.

The Van Eeghen sketchbook is the focus of a display in the museum from August 19 until November 29.

World.title: Holidaymakers warned not to bring home “destructive” beetle
World.content:
The Dutch food standards watchdog NVWA has urged returning holidaymakers not to bring back foreign invaders after a Japanese beetle was found in a freight shipment from Italy.

The insect was found dead in a plastic container that was being transported from a region of Italy where Japanese beetles are known to live.

The NVWA set traps in the container to see if any live beetles had crept inside, but none were found. But the agency told people coming back from southern Europe and transport companies to be alert and report any specimens they found.

“The NVWA is explicitly asking trading and logistics companies to be alert for beetles hitching a lift when they travel to or through the named areas,” the agency said in a statement.

“Do not in any event leave the doors and windows of your vehicle open for longer than necessary and try to check goods and packing for beetles before departure if possible.“

Japanese beetles are not considered a pest in their native country, where their numbers are controlled by natural predators.

But in recent years they have been spotted in Italy, Croatia, Switzerland, Germany and the Azores. The German province of Hessen is the closest area to the Netherlands with an established population.

They are regarded as highly destructive because they feed on a wide range of vegetation. Adult beetles will devour leaves and stems of plants, while their larvae eat grass roots and weeds.

The NVWA has also published advice on its website advising people how to tell Japanese beetles apart from similar looking native species.

World.title: Inflation making plant-based foods cheaper than meat and dairy
World.content:
Plant-based foods now cost less than meat and dairy equivalents at nine major supermarkets in the Netherlands, according to new research published by food organisation ProVeg.

“It’s remarkable that this is happening,” Martine van Haperen, nutrition and health expert at ProVeg, told DutchNews.

“It’s normally been very difficult for plant-based products to compete with animal-based ones. What we’re seeing now is that store brands like Albert Heijn have expanded their own-brand products, making them more affordable.”

The bigger driver, she said, is inflation. “Inflation has hit animal products much harder than plant-based ones, and that is because animal products require much more resources to be produced.”

Cheaper across the board

ProVeg, which has tracked the price gap since 2022, compared the cheapest plant-based version of each product with the cheapest animal one, priced per kilo, at nine chains in late April.

A basic basket of six items stocked everywhere – mince, burgers, butter, milk, yoghurt and cheese – was cheaper in its plant-based form at every chain, by around 18% on average.

Shoppers buying staples such as mince and milk can save up to 30%, the organisation said, with the widest gaps at Plus and Dirk and the narrowest at the organic chain Ekoplaza. Plant-based butter came in 48% cheaper.

The plant-based versions of some products remain far more expensive, however: mayonnaise costs almost four times as much as the animal version, while vegan yoghurt and kwark are both more than double the price.

The bigger basket

ProVeg also compared a wider basket of 14 products – adding items such as sausages, shoarma and mayonnaise that not every chain sells in a plant-based version. On that fuller list the plant-based basket costs more at four shops: Dirk, Hoogvliet, Jumbo and Picnic. At Albert Heijn the two come out level.

Dirk is the odd one out, with its plant-based basics are among the cheapest of any chain, but its wider basket ends up 25% more expensive than the meat one. It stocks a plant-based version in all 14 categories – just not a cheap own-brand in every one, and those pricier extras drag the total up.

World.title: Police get stop and search powers after shootings in Zuidoost
World.content:
Police will be able to stop and search anyone for weapons in part of Amsterdam-Zuidoost for a week from Thursday, after a long series of shooting and gun threats that the city says often involve minors.

The mayor, police and public prosecutor have designated the H-buurt, the K-buurt and the Nelson Mandelapark a security risk area until August 27. Inside it, police can search people without having any specific cause for suspicion.

Authorities recorded 18 firearm-related incidents in the area between June 1 and August 1, ranging from threats made at gunpoint to shootings that left people wounded.

In one case on August 3, a shot fired during a confrontation passed through a wall into a child’s bedroom. A minor was inside the house at the time, reported local broadcaster AT5.

Second summer running

It is the second summer in a row that Zuidoost has faced such a regime. Last year’s designation followed the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old and was extended into September.

Extra police patrols had already been deployed this summer, the city said, but had not been enough to restore calm.

Controversial tactics

Preventive searching has been used in Rotterdam for a long time. It was introduced there in 2002 and now covers large parts of Rotterdam-Zuid.

The tactic is controversial, with opposition and coalition parties on Rotterdam’s council having accused the city of ethnic profiling. Stop and searches in Rotterdam require at least three police officers at every search to guard against it.

Amsterdam dropped preventive searching in 2015, deeming it ineffective. The city has still used it repeatedly over the past year, in the red light district, over New Year and now twice in Zuidoost.

Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she came to parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is the main opponent of PiS. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.title: FedEx-led €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost wins EU approval
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and whom Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Prague’s Groovy Market Fest Returns After a Successful Debut
World.content:
A new urban festival is aiming to become a regular fixture on Prague’s cultural calendar after attracting 1,200 visitors to its first edition in Riegrovy sady.

Groovy Market Fest, held on August 1, brought together food, design, music and local brands in a format inspired by European city markets.

According to the organizers, around 85% of visitors were tourists or foreign residents of Prague, highlighting the event’s appeal beyond the Czech-speaking audience.



The festival will return to Riegrovy sady on September 5, with further editions planned for October, November and December.

From Barcelona to Prague

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food culture.

Their interest in international gastronomy also led them to compete in Spain. In 2025, they won first place in the Cooking The Street competition, where their dish was judged by a professional panel that included chefs Beñat Ormaetxea and Jon Kepa Aurrecoetxea.

After returning to Prague, they decided to develop their own event, drawing inspiration from markets such as Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market.

The First Edition

Food Garden focused on gastronomy, while Palm Street featured local products and handmade goods. The Design Zone presented Czech brands working in fashion, design and art.

Rather than filling the site with as many vendors as possible, the organizers selected a smaller number of participants. They say the approach was intended to create a more coherent experience for visitors.

Music was another part of the programme, with live performances and DJ sets throughout the event. Visitors could also attend a masterclass focused on preparing the festival’s signature Groovy cocktail.

Additional editions are scheduled for October 3, November 7 and December 5, all at the same location.

Tickets for upcoming editions are available through GoOut.

World.title: Faster Than the Metro. New Bus is Now Linking Prague 8 and Prague 6
World.content:
A new bus service running through Prague’s Blanka tunnel has begun operating, offering a direct connection between the northern part of the city and Dejvice.

Bus line 145 connects Čimice and Kobylisy in Prague 8 with Hradčanská and Dejvická in Prague 6. The journey takes around 15 minutes, according to Prague’s public transport authority ROPID.



The same trip by metro requires a change between lines C and A in the city centre and takes around 22 minutes.

Including the time spent walking through stations and using escalators, the journey can take about half an hour.

The first day of operation brought mostly positive results, with many buses arriving on time or even ahead of schedule. The real test will come during regular weekday traffic, when congestion around Prague is heavier.

Where the new bus runs

In the direction from Čimice to Dejvice, line 145 serves:

Sídliště Čimice – Čimice – Libeňská – Řepínská – Podhajská pole – Čimický háj – Písečná – Služská – Kobylisy – Okrouhlická – Vychovatelna – Hradčanská – Vítězné náměstí – Dejvická

The return route follows the same corridor in the opposite direction.

The key feature of line 145 is its use of the Blanka tunnel, allowing buses to avoid the city centre and provide a direct connection between Prague 8 and Prague 6.

The new route is expected to make commuting easier for residents of Čimice, Kobylisy and surrounding neighbourhoods, while providing an alternative to the metro for journeys towards Dejvice and Hradčanská.

World.title: Leo Express to Launch Direct Prague–Brno Trains in December
World.content:
Leo Express is set to begin operating direct trains between Prague and Brno in December, marking the private carrier’s first direct connection between the two cities.

The company has already been serving passengers in the South Moravian Region, but its trains have so far bypassed Brno.

Over the past year, travellers from towns such as Hodonín and Břeclav have been able to use Leo Express services to reach Prague, travelling via Přerov and Olomouc.



The new Prague–Brno service will change that, putting the carrier directly on one of the Czech Republic’s busiest rail routes.

There is, however, one limitation for passengers travelling to Prague.

Leo Express trains do not serve Prague Main Station. In Prague, passengers must use Praha-Libeň station, which may be less convenient for those travelling to the city centre.

Leo Express was founded by businessman Leoš Novotný and has operated passenger trains in the Czech Republic since 2012.

The company has gradually expanded its network in the Czech Republic and abroad, competing with established operators such as České dráhy and RegioJet.

The Prague–Brno connection is expected to become another important part of the company’s Czech network from December.

World.title: Romanian Community to Celebrate Culture and Traditions in Prague
World.content:
The Romanian community in Czechia will come together in Prague on September 6 for the 12th edition of the Romanian Celebration, an annual event highlighting Romanian culture, traditions and the community’s ties with Czech society.

The main event will take place at the Ethnographic Section of the National Museum of the Czech Republic in Kinský Park, Prague 5.

The program will bring together Romanian music, dance, food, literature and activities for children.



Organized by the Association of Romanians in the Czech Republic (ARRC), the event is part of a wider cultural project running from March 1 to November 30, 2026.

Visitors can expect traditional music and dance performances, educational activities for children, cultural exhibitions, book presentations and Romanian gastronomy.

The event is aimed at members of the Romanian community, Romanian-speaking families, children and young people, as well as Czech residents interested in Romanian culture.

According to ARRC, the project aims to preserve and promote Romanian cultural and linguistic identity among Romanians living in the Czech Republic while creating opportunities for greater interaction between the Romanian and Czech communities.

“Through this project, we aim to offer the Romanian community, Romanian speakers, and lovers of the Romanian language a space for meeting, dialogue, and celebration of our cultural values, while also contributing to the consolidation of intercultural relations between Romania and the Czech Republic,” the ARRC leadership said.

World.title: Czech Fish Farmers Take Emergency Measures Amid Prolonged Drought
World.content:
Fish farmers reduce or suspend supplementary feeding to lower oxygen consumption, reports say.

Fish farmers in the Czech Republic have begun taking emergency measures as a prolonged drought, worsened by high temperatures across Europe, strains water supplies.

Facing water shortages, fish farmers have reduced or suspended supplementary feeding to lower fish oxygen consumption, while ponds are being regularly aerated, according to the report.



Several ponds have also been netted earlier than usual.

In the Třeboň area, which delivers tons of carp for the Czech Christmas table, part of the 200-hectare Koclířov pond has been drained and the fish moved to holding tanks.

More than a third of the water is missing from the region’s famous system of fish ponds due to the drought. The water level in Lake Svět, for example, has fallen by 98 centimetres. High temperatures are also causing water to evaporate more quickly.

The Czech government is expected to address the 2027 budget, upcoming elections and measures to tackle worsening drought.

Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has pledged an extra CZK 4 billion for drought-related measures. If approved, ministers will present plans for implementing them.

World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: How Much Can a Prague Taxi Driver Really Earn Each Month
World.content:
For passengers, a taxi ride can make the job look straightforward. Pick someone up, drive them across Prague, wait for the next booking and repeat.

But the income of a full-time taxi driver depends on far more than the fare shown on the meter or app.

Drivers working through platforms such as Uber and Bolt can generate more than CZK 60,000 in gross monthly revenue when working around 40 to 50 hours a week. What they actually keep, however, is considerably less.



Gross income can exceed CZK 60,000

Official figures for Prague’s taxi sector put the average gross monthly pay at roughly CZK 38,000. Drivers who work full time through ride-hailing platforms can earn more, particularly when they concentrate on periods of high demand.

According to Ondřej Krátký, founder of the Czech taxi platform Liftago, drivers can typically earn about CZK 250 to CZK 350 per hour. At the lower end of the market, however, some drivers make only around CZK 80 an hour, which is difficult to turn into a sustainable income in Prague.

Official statistics may also underestimate the money generated by some drivers because not every journey is paid through an app. Cash payments remain part of the business.

Fuel and commissions take a large share

Most Prague taxi drivers operate as self-employed contractors and use their own cars. That means they are responsible for almost all of the costs associated with the job.

Fuel is one of the largest expenses. Someone driving every day can spend more than CZK 10,000 a month on petrol or diesel alone.

Ride-hailing platforms also take a percentage of each fare. Depending on the service and other conditions, commissions can account for roughly 20 to 25 percent of the fare. Drivers must also cover vehicle maintenance, repairs, commercial insurance and the mandatory social and health insurance payments required of self-employed workers.

Once these expenses are taken into account, the amount left from gross earnings can fall by a third or more.

For a full-time driver, a realistic monthly amount after operating costs can therefore be somewhere between CZK 22,000 and CZK 35,000. The exact figure depends on the car, fuel consumption, working hours, platform commissions and the number and type of trips completed.

Tips make only a small difference

Tips are unlikely to transform a taxi driver’s income in the Czech Republic.

Unlike in countries where tipping is a major part of service workers’ earnings, Czech passengers generally round up the fare or leave a relatively small amount.

Uber allows passengers to tip through its app for up to 30 days after a journey, with the full tip going to the driver. Bolt offers a similar feature.

For most drivers, however, tips remain a minor addition to their monthly income rather than a significant source of earnings.

Timing can make a bigger difference

Drivers can increase their income by choosing when and where they work.

Friday and Saturday nights are among the busiest periods in Prague, particularly in the city centre. When demand rises sharply, ride-hailing platforms can increase fares, allowing drivers to generate more revenue from the same number of working hours.

Major concerts, festivals and other large events can have a similar effect. Airport journeys can also be attractive because they tend to cover longer distances than short trips within the city.

World.title: Popular Hungarian dairy and food brand Cserpes has a new owner
World.content:
Family-owned cheese maker Profood Flexum has acquired local peer Cserpes Sajtműhely Élelmiszeripari Ltd, the company’s brand consultant told MTI.

No details discolosed about Cserpes transaction

The sides did not disclose the details of the transaction which includes Cserpes‘s entire vertically integrated business. No changes will be made to the brand, its products, its network of shops or its staff.

“The goal is to preserve, further develop and strengthen a successful Hungarian brand,” the statement said. Founder István Cserpes will continue to advise on the brand and play an active role in its future development, MTI wrote.

Profood Flexum operates its own farm and dairy. It counts SAGA, Gallicoop, Spar, Merian Foods, CBA and the pizzeria Don Pepe among its business partners.

A 30+ yo brand

Cserpes Sajtműhely was founded by István Cserpes in 1992. Its products include milk, yoghurt, cheese and Cserpes Trudi. The first Cserpes Tejivó opened in 2012, and the company currently operates three milk bars in Budapest.

Since 2013, the Cserpes brand has received MagyarBrands recognition and has been entitled to display the Superbrands trademark. In 2025, István Cserpes received the Entrepreneur of the Year award from the National Association of Entrepreneurs and Employers.

Last year, Cserpes recorded revenue of HUF 5.073 billion and a post-tax profit of HUF 367 million. In 2024, its revenue stood at HUF 4.5 billion and its profit at HUF 652 million. The company employs approximately 200 people.

World.title: Were foreign students in Hungary Orbán’s next target? Influencer suffers a spectacular backlash
World.content:
A group of “headscarf-wearing women and black men” got off a Hungarian-registered bus at a rest stop near the country’s western border. That was all it took for Virág Gulyás, a journalist and influencer for Mandiner, one of the Orbán regime’s flagship media outlets, to suggest that Péter Magyar had begun the mass resettlement of illegal migrants. It apparently did not occur to her that they might be foreign students.

Fidesz influencer’s narrative fits neatly into Orbán’s propaganda

“There isn’t much of a tourism branding angle on that bus,” Gulyás wrote, swiftly concluding that the passengers could not be tourists and must instead be illegal migrants.

These, of course, are the people against whom the Orbán government claims to have taken action, building a border fence and spending roughly a decade frightening the public with warnings that, unless Fidesz remained in power, the country would be overrun by immigrants.

That narrative only partly reflected reality. The migrants who gathered at Budapest’s Keleti railway station and along the motorways in 2015 were not trying to enter Hungary; they wanted to travel west. Their bottleneck was caused precisely by the closure of Hungary’s western borders.

Since the change of government, it has emerged that the Orbán administration had planned to build a refugee camp in Vitnyéd. It had also long been known that the government had admitted large numbers of guest workers, who have since become indispensable in certain sectors as Hungarian workers have emigrated.

Meanwhile, Péter Magyar has been repeatedly attacked for allegedly welcoming illegal migrants. The Tisza government, however, has consistently made its position clear: it would reject the admission and subsidisation of migrants, maintain the fence along Hungary’s southern border, and co-operate with the European Union in addressing a problem that affects several countries.

Fidesz-linked influencer immediately mistook foreign students for illegal immigrants

Ms Gulyás’s post fitted the Fidesz propaganda machine perfectly. She claimed that a Hungarian-registered bus was carrying “headscarf-wearing women and black men” near Sopron, as though an organised programme of mass settlement had already begun.

Are Orbán’s next target foreign students learning in Hungary? Photo: Facebook/Gulyás Virág kimondja

The National Conference of Student Unions (HÖOK) responded, however, and clarified that the passengers were students enrolled in the Stipendium Hungaricum programme, launched by the Orbán government in 2013.

They were in Hungary to study and, on returning home, to use the knowledge they had acquired for the benefit of their own countries. They were also expected to remember the generosity of the Hungarian state, which provides scholarships and other forms of support, form lifelong friendships and professional relationships, and thereby help advance Hungary’s national and foreign-policy objectives while improving the country’s image abroad.

Leaked: Fidesz could be dismantled within weeks as its fate rests with members – and János Lázár

HÖOK said that more than 11,000 students were studying in Hungary under the programme this year. The students pictured had been visiting Sopron, where they learned about a wide range of subjects, from the city’s Roman remains and its famous referendum to its rich student traditions, the origins of the Hungarian people and the foundation of the Hungarian state.

Let us hope they took plenty away from the trip — and that the Fidesz influencer’s insulting post did not reach them.

Lots of foreign students acquire their degree in Hungary. Illustration. Photo: Facebook/BME

Rather than apologise, however, Ms Gulyás insulted HÖOK over its response and angrily declared that, although the organisation had now offered an explanation, she would continue photographing every suspicious-looking bus and bringing the matter to public attention.

She even appealed to her 182,000 followers, asking them to send her more pictures of a similar nature.
